questions.question: State and prove the Maximum Modulus Principle / [CO1, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• State and prove the Maximum Modulus Principle.[An] / [CO1, CO4]
  • •Ans:Statement:If a functionfis analytic and not constant in a given domain D, then|f(z)|has no maximum value inD. 2 marks Proof: –SinceRis closed and bounded and|f(z)|is continuous onR,|f(z)|attains a maximumMat some pointz 0 ∈R. –Supposez 0 is an interior point ofR. Then there exists a disk|z−z 0| ≤ρlying entirely insideR. –By Gauss’s Mean Value Theorem: f(z 0) = 12π ∫︂ 2π0 f(z 0 +ρe iθ)dθ 4 marks –Taking absolute values: |f(z 0)| ≤12π ∫︂ 2π0 |f(z 0 +ρe iθ)|dθ≤ 12π ∫︂ 2π0 M dθ=M –Since|f(z 0)|=M, we have: 1 2π ∫︂ 2π 0 [M− |f(z0 +ρe iθ)|]dθ= 0 –SinceM− |f(z 0 +ρe iθ)| ≥0 and is continuous,|f(z)|=Mfor all points on |z−z 0|=ρ. –Since this holds for allr≤ρ,|f(z)|=Mthroughout the disk. An analytic function with constant modulus is constant. –Thus, iff(z) is non-constant,|f(z)|cannot attain its maximum in the interior and must occur on the boundary. 4 marks – 7 Marks are to be awarded for the proof according to the discretion of the evaluator.
